linkedin.post:
About 35%: how far Nvidia's shares fell from October's record close to Monday's close, as Jensen Huang's exit shook the AI chipmaker.

Huang quit as CEO last week amid a board inquiry. Now he says he "would be honored" to return if asked. A source told CNBC the board isn't considering it. Interim CEO Colette Kress delivers her first results this morning, Australian time, and Bloomberg Intelligence says his exit needn't change earnings forecasts.

If Nvidia holds up without him, should the board bring back the founder who quit in scandal? Tell us what you think below.

#AusSight #AI

warnings: Nvidia's Q3 FY2027 results were not yet published when this package was made (due 8:20am AEDT Wed 18 Nov). The video and posts say the results 'land this morning, Australian time' and do not state any result figures. Do not add result figures to the posts unless verified.

Share prices are US$ New York closes: record close $239.24 on 6 Oct 2026 (Euronews, single source) and $156.10 on Mon 16 Nov 2026 (Yahoo Finance, single source); the ~35% fall is calculated from those two closes. Tuesday 17 Nov close not included.
'Board not considering bringing him back' rests on an unnamed source reported by CNBC on 16 Nov (US), also reported by Forbes; it is attributed as such.
Video runs 56.8s, above the 40-50s target but within the 60s maximum.
notes: Story picked at about 7am AEDT. Huang's quote is from his written statement of 17 Nov (US), as reported by Fox Business and Forbes; the full statement text was not available, so only the reported words are used. No financial advice; analyst view attributed to Bloomberg Intelligence (Kunjan Sobhani, via Euronews). The scandal is described only as a board inquiry and resignation; no allegations about other people are named. No verified Australian-specific angle was found (an AustralianSuper Nvidia holding figure was single-source and undated, so left out). Cover files: cover.png and cover-vertical.png, built on the Commons photo of Jensen Huang (Anders Eidesvik, CC BY-SA 4.0). Wikimedia Commons was heavily rate-limited: the Nvidia headquarters photos and a landscape Huang photo could not be downloaded, so file footage of chips, New York and markets was used; the Kress photo is a 2017 still and is labelled 'File photo, 2017'.
